Priya (Security): Quick question from the customer's security team — they want to confirm POC KMS details before we kick off. Specifically: can Redwood support HSM-backed keys (BYOK) for the POC, what level of control do they get over rotation, and is key material ever exportable?
Diego (Solutions): @Priya we can do HSM-backed BYOK for Dedicated and Private. For hosted (Redwood-managed) we offer envelope encryption with customer-provided KMS references (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) but not raw key import. For BYOK with HSM import we recommend Private or Dedicated where customer controls the KMS.
Ava (Account Exec): Customer asked about timeline — they want BYOK during the 2-week POC. Is that feasible?
Sam (Infra): 2 weeks is fine if they can provision the key in their cloud KMS and share an arn/identifier + grant us decrypt/encrypt IAM role. If they want to import key material into an HSM (CloudHSM) that usually takes longer (key import, attestation). Depends on their compliance team.
Priya (Security): Important: they require non-exportability and HSM attestation (FIPS 140-2 L3). Can Redwood confirm we don't persist plaintext keys and that we only store KMS references? Also need to know rotation flexibility (customer-driven vs Redwood-managed).
Diego (Solutions): We do NOT persist plaintext key material. For Private/Dedicated with customer-managed KMS, Redwood stores only the KMS key reference and uses the customer's KMS to perform envelope encryption ops. Rotation: customer-managed keys = customer controls rotation and Redwood will pick up new key identifiers if they reconfigure; we can also support a rotation workflow where customer rotates and updates arn in the POC conf. For hosted customers wanting us to manage rotation, we can do scheduled rotations but keys remain within Redwood's managed KMS (not HSM).
Ava (Account Exec): Pricing question from procurement: is there an additional charge for HSM-backed BYOK during POC? They expect a line item.
Diego (Solutions): For POC we usually absorb one-off operational cost, but if HSM provisioning or attestation requires vendor fees we'll pass those along. For Dedicated/Private there is the standard Dedicated commit + add-on for increased key management retention/audit (we can provide exact SKU). I'll follow up with pricing numbers.
Priya (Security): Security questionnaire items: they want proof of HSM attestation and KMS audit logs (access & crypto ops). Can we produce a short attestation package for POC?
Sam (Infra): We can provide KMS audit logs if the key lives in customer's KMS (they already have logs in CloudTrail/Stackdriver). For Redwood-managed keys we can provide our audit trail extract (who requested what, timestamps) but attestation certs belong to the HSM provider (we can surface the provider artifacts). For Private deployments we can run local attestation and hand over the report.
Diego (Solutions): To keep the POC moving, here's the minimal checklist I need from the customer: 1) target deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) 2) KMS provider and whether they will import key material 3) required compliance certs (e.g., FIPS 140-2 L3) 4) rotation policy (days) 5) contact for KMS/IAM setup
Ava (Account Exec): I'll ask them for answers. Can we provide a short config snippet they can paste to grant Redwood access? That speeds things up.
Sam (Infra): Yep — here's a sample AWS IAM + KMS policy snippet they can attach to the role we use (replace placeholders):
```json
{ "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Sid": "AllowRedwoodUse", "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-poc-role"}, "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:DescribeKey"], "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/EXAMPLE-KEY-ID" } ] }
```
Priya (Security): Good. Also need to confirm key lifecycle: if they delete the KMS key, what happens to stored artifacts? Do we proactively refuse to decrypt and flag data unavailable?
Diego (Solutions): If customer deletes the key in their KMS, any ciphertext we stored encrypted under that key becomes irretrievable — we will surface errors and mark the dataset as inaccessible. We recommend versioned key rotation rather than deletion for recoverability during POC.
Ava (Account Exec): Customer also asked if Redwood can sign an SLA clause around non-exportability during the POC. Legal will need the exact wording — do we have standard contract language for BYOK where we state we never access plaintext and do not export key material?
Priya (Security): We have standard BYOK language in the enterprise template. I'll pull the clause and drop it here.
ops-bot: Reminder: create a POC ticket with label "BYOK-HSM" and attach checklist.
Diego (Solutions): Thanks @ops-bot — next steps: Ava, get the answers to the checklist + their preferred KMS arn. Priya/Sam we'll prepare attestation/clauses to drop into the SOW. I'll flag pricing follow-up for Dedicated/Private HSM add-ons.
Ava (Account Exec): On it. I'll update this thread when I have the KMS arn. :thumbsup:
Priya (Security): If they need an accelerated attestation we can request the vendor's cert but that might add 2-3 days. Calling that out now.
Diego (Solutions): Perfect — closing loop here. If anything blocks the 2-week POC start date we'll triage immediately.
Ava (Account Exec): FYI customer prefers AWS CloudHSM and wants rotation every 90 days. I'll confirm import vs. KMS-generated key today.
Sam (Infra): Noted. If they insist on CloudHSM import we should budget extra for HSM key import + attestation steps.
Priya (Security): Thanks all — this helps.
